item.title: What Are U.S. Military Options in Iran?
item.description: As Washington weighs force against Tehran alongside ongoing negotiations and an economic blockade, CSIS’s Benjamin Jensen evaluates six military options ranging from coercive diplomacy and targeted strikes to a prolonged sea control campaign and covert action.

item.title: Who Controls Ukraine’s Starlink Access?
item.description: A 100 mph speed limit on Starshield terminals hindered Ukraine’s efforts to intercept Russia’s jet-powered drones. The risk of losing access during an attack gives allies another reason to build their own networks instead of buying service from U.S. companies.

item.title: Strength in Unity: Climate Action for the Pacific Islands
item.description: Pacific Island countries have turned collective diplomacy into global climate influence—but there are limits to this approach without greater global support.

item.title: Transshipment Crackdowns Won’t Fix the U.S.-China Trade Imbalance
item.description: The White House alleges that Chinese exports are being rerouted through third countries to circumvent U.S. tariffs. By analyzing transshipment activity and substantive supply chain shifts, CSIS challenges this diagnosis and highlights persistent structural issues.

item.title: What Latin America Can Teach the United States about Drone Defense
item.description: The CSIS Americas Program analyzes opportunities for the United States to cooperate with partners in Latin America to combat nonstate drone threats.

item.title: Only the Gulf Can End the Iran War
item.description: In Foreign Affairs, CSIS's Allison Minor with Nate Swanson argues a cease-fire brokered and managed by the Gulf Arab states can end the Iran war.

item.title: FY 2027 Defense Funding: Potential Post-Midterm Outcomes
item.description: Congress has a full post-midterm agenda, with action needed to fund the Department of Defense and federal government and reconciliation legislation to consider. Seamus Daniels lays out the factors that will shape FY 2027 defense funding decisions after the midterms.

item.title: Decoding the Right-to-Repair Debate
item.description: The right-to-repair debate, concerning who controls U.S. defense IP, has become a contentious issue in defense acquisition policy. Lawmakers need to balance the military’s push for greater access to technical data and industry’s fear of losing revenue and IP control.
